narrative:
The 2020 New York Mets entered the pandemic-shortened 60-game season with high hopes, boasting a potent offense and a bullpen headlined by flamethrower Edwin Díaz. But from the very first week, the cracks were visible. A brutal July saw the Mets drop to 3-5, with Díaz immediately establishing himself as a liability — surrendering a homer to Marcell Ozuna in the season's opening days and setting the tone for a bullpen that would repeatedly squander leads.

August told a more complicated story. The Mets surged to a 12-15 record, finding moments of genuine brilliance amid the chaos. Michael Conforto's two-run blast on August 19th and Amed Rosario's clutch homer on August 28th offered glimpses of the offense's potential, while Robinson Canó chipped in timely hits that kept the team afloat. Yet the era was defined by devastating collapses — none more painful than the August 30th debacle against the Yankees, when Díaz imploded and Drew Smith surrendered a Gary Sánchez grand slam, turning what might have been a rivalry statement into a symbol of institutional dysfunction.

September brought a final push that ultimately came up short. The Mets went 11-14 over the final stretch, manufacturing just enough drama — J.D. Davis's solo shot on September 3rd, Jeff McNeil's three-run blast on September 7th, Brandon Nimmo's homer on September 17th — to tantalize but never truly contend. Miguel Castro's inability to protect leads mirrored the bullpen's season-long failures, and the Mets finished 26-34, well outside the expanded playoff field.

The 2020 Mets were a team perpetually undone by their own relief corps. With a solid .807 team OPS, the offense generated enough to compete on most nights, but a 4.98 ERA told the real story: the pitching staff, particularly in high-leverage situations, gave games away faster than the bats could win them back. Edwin Díaz alone appeared in two of the season's most damaging moments, and the bullpen as a whole became a nightly source of dread for a fanbase that had hoped this would be a year of resurgence.

chapters.title: Rough Out of the Gate
chapters.description: The Mets stumble through a brutal July, with early bullpen failures setting a troubling tone for the shortened season.

chapters.title: August Sparks
chapters.description: Offensive heroes like Conforto and Rosario ignite a winning stretch that keeps the Mets in contention despite persistent bullpen woes.

chapters.title: The Yankee Nightmare
chapters.description: A single catastrophic August 30th collapse against the Yankees — featuring multiple Díaz meltdowns and a Sánchez grand slam — encapsulates everything wrong with this Mets team.

chapters.title: Too Little, Too Late
chapters.description: Davis, McNeil, and Nimmo deliver clutch September moments, but the Mets cannot overcome their season-long deficits and fall short of the expanded playoffs.
